intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene on chromosome 10q23-q24.

paragraphs.text: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia that mainly affects the spine. Features include short stature, platyspondyly or rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular end plates and narrow intervertebral spaces, mild brachydactyly or mildly shortened metacarpals, and epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones that are mild and vary between patients (Ahmad et al., 1998; Miyake et al., 2012). Miyake et al. (2012) concluded that PAPSS2 mutations cause a family of skeletal dysplasias whose phenotypes range from brachyolmia to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. Because PAPSS2 deficiency also impairs sulfation of DHEA, a girl with compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations had premature pubarche and androgen excess (Noordam et al., 2009).

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large inbred kindred from a remote area of Pakistan, spanning 8 generations, with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. They evaluated 16 affected individuals (11 males and 5 females). Clinical findings included short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence. Radiographs showed delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees, platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces, diffuse early osteoarthritic changes mainly in the spine and hands, and mild brachydactyly. Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen mainly at the hips and knees. The authors considered this phenotype distinct from other autosomal recessive forms of SEMD because of the mild metaphyseal involvement, the type of brachydactyly, and the absence of loose joints or other clinical findings.

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) studied 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia and 3 patients with similar phenotypes (2 Japanese and 1 Korean). All 6 patients had short-trunk short stature that became obvious during childhood, with normal intelligence and facies. Radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular end plates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of the rib cartilages, short femoral neck, and mildly shortened metacarpals. Spinal changes were very similar in all 6 patients, but epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones varied.

paragraphs.text: In 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia, Miyake et al. (2012) used exon capture followed by next-generation sequencing and identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the PAPSS2 gene (c.337_338insG; p.A113GfsX18). In 3 further patients with similar brachyolmia phenotypes (2 Japanese and 1 Korean), they also found loss-of-function mutations in PAPSS2. One patient was homozygous for an IVS3+2delT mutation. The second was compound heterozygous for c.616_634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309_1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19). The third was compound heterozygous for c.480_481insCGTA (p.K161RfsX6) and c.661delA (p.I221SfsX40).
